review.method_name: Kramers-Kronig PAM transceiver and two-sided polarization-multiplexed Kramers-Kronig (TS-KK) transceiver
experimental_conditions: KK-PAM numerical validation over 100 km SSMF using 48-Gbaud 4-PAM and roll-off 0.05
KK-PAM simulations used a 26 dB loss budget and 5 dB noise figure
TS-KK simulation transmitted two 48-Gbaud 4-ASK signals through five 100 km spans
TS-KK simulation used 80 GHz WDM spacing and an 8.6 GHz frequency gap
main_results: KK-PAM reconstructs optical phase and enables digital chromatic-dispersion compensation
For 500 km propagation, TS-KK BER remained below 10^-3 in the evaluated cases
TS-KK needs four photodiodes and no optical hybrids, compared with eight photodiodes and two optical hybrids for an intradyne receiver
